targetWords.definition: An arrow is a thin, straight stick shot from a bow.
targetWords.example: The arrow flew through the air and hit the target.

targetWords.definition: A battle is a fight between two armies during a war.
targetWords.example: ■The battle lasted for many days.

targetWords.definition: A bow is a weapon made of curved wood and string that shoots arrows.
targetWords.example: ■He went hunting with a bow and arrow.

targetWords.definition: When people are brave, they are not afraid to face pain or danger.
targetWords.example: The brave firefighter saved the girl from the burning building.

targetWords.definition: A chief is the leader of a group of people.
targetWords.example: The chief led the people through the mountains.

targetWords.definition: A disadvantage is a situation where someone is likely to lose.
targetWords.example: ■Mike had a disadvantage in the race since he hurt his knee.

targetWords.definition: An enemy is a country that is fighting another country during a war.
targetWords.example: The enemy prepared to attack the kingdom.

targetWords.definition: An entrance is a place where someone can enter an area.
targetWords.example: The gate was locked, so Bill had to find a different entrance.

targetWords.definition: If something hardly happens, it almost does not happen at all.
targetWords.example: I hardly saw the concert since I had to leave early.

targetWords.definition: To intend to do something means to plan to do it.
targetWords.example: I intend to finish college in three years.

targetWords.definition: Laughter is the sound produced by laughing about something funny.
targetWords.example: Susan's joke made her classmates burst into laughter.

targetWords.definition: A log is a thick piece of wood that is cut from a tree.
targetWords.example: The fire was too small, so we added another log to it.

targetWords.definition: The military is the armed forces of a country.
targetWords.example: I joined the m ilitary after I finished high school.

targetWords.definition: To obey means to follow what a law or a person says you must do.
targetWords.example: My little sister did not obey my mother. Now she is in trouble.

targetWords.definition: To secure something means to get it after a lot of effort.
targetWords.example: I was able to secure a good grade on my test after weeks ofstudying.

targetWords.definition: When someone or something is steady, they are under control.
targetWords.example: The problem was hard but she remained steady and solved it.

targetWords.definition: To trust is to believe that someone is honest and will do what is right.
targetWords.example: I trust my friends; they don't tell my secrets to other people.

targetWords.definition: To twist something is to wrap it around itself or another thing.
targetWords.example: ■She twisted the spaghetti around her fork.

targetWords.definition: Unless means if not or except when.
targetWords.example: ■Unless you clean your room, you cannot play with your friends. weapon [wepan] n.

targetWords.example: ■Swords have been used as weapons for thousands of years.

story.title: The Battle of Thermopylae
story.passage:
This is a true story. It happened long ago in Greece___

"We must fight," the Spartan* chief told his small army of brave men. They

were at a great disadvantage. There were only three hundred of them. The Persian

military had hundreds of thousands of men.

They were going to lose unless they could secure a small entrance. The enemy

couldn't move through it easily. They intended to stop the enemy here. The chief

and his men got ready for the battle.

Soon, long lines of the enemy's army twisted around the hills. The chief met the

enemy with laughter. He knew that his men's weapons and skills were better. The

Spartans trusted their leader and obeyed him.

First, the enemy soldiers shot arrows from their bows. The chief told his men

to lift their shields*. The arrows stuck into the shields but did not hurt any of the

men.

Then the enemy's soldiers attacked the Spartans with long spears. The chief

surprised them. His troops rolled logs down on the enemy.

They fought for three days. Though they hardly slept at all,

the chief and his men remained steady.

But the enemy found a way to beat the Spartans. The

chief and all of his men were killed. Even though they

lost, the Battle ofThermopylae is one of the most famous

battles in history.

* Spartan - a soldier from the city of

Sparta in Greece

* shield - a piece of wood or metal that

soldiers carried to protect themselves

questions.question: Why was the smaller army not afraid of the larger one?

options.text: The larger army didn't have any weapons.
The smaller army had better weapons and skills.
The larger army did not trust their leader.
The smaller army did not intend to fight.

options.text: because they heard the soldiers' laughter
unless they secured the narrow entrance
against the other army's bows and arrows
hardly any men fighting the large army

options.text: their long lines of soldiers twisted around the hills
they had a steady three-day attack against the Spartans
they used fire to defeat the Spartans
